reader.requirement: At --std 85, in MOVE Format 1 the sender is literal-1 (a literal, figurative constant or ALL literal) or identifier-1 (a data item, a reference modification, an alphanumeric function-identifier; no 2002 inline method invocation, no numeric function outside an arithmetic expression) and every identifier-2 is a receiving data item (subscripted, reference-modified, a special register such as PAGE-COUNTER) and never a literal, a figurative constant or a function-identifier; each receiver gets the sender in turn.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the identifier-1 Format 4 inline method invocation (obj :: "m") below 2002
below 2002 refuses a numeric/integer function-identifier as MOVE identifier-1 (construct numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002, §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4)
the 2002 data-address-identifier receiver (ADDRESS OF) is not a word at 85, so 'MOVE P TO ADDRESS OF N' is an undefined name (COBOL1639)

reader.edition-search: the sender/receiver split itself is the grammar (moveStatement: MOVE sendingOperand moveReceivingPhrase, receivingIdentifier admits no literal or functionCall) and consults no edition; the edition arms above were found from the witnesses' COBOL0900 messages and from probing the 2002 forms
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 identifier-1 may not be an inline method invocation or a numeric/integer function, and identifier-2 may not be ADDRESS OF; the sending/receiving roles are the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the 2002 inline invocation refusal and PAGE-COUNTER as receiver; a literal, figurative or function-identifier written as identifier-2, several receivers and reference modification at the bounds were not exercised by them

probes.expected: two receivers truncated/padded; alphanumeric function sender; ALL literal; X(6:1) and Z(3:) receivers at their bounds; ODO receiver at 2 and 5; numeric literal to numeric

probes.printed: COBOL5506 unexpected '"ABC"' ... no literal is expected at this position
probes.expected: refused: identifier-2 cannot be a literal
refused: a figurative constant is no receiving area
refused: a function-identifier is no receiving area

probes.printed: COBOL0900 a numeric or integer function-identifier where an identifier is written ... requires COBOL-2002

probes.expected: refused: no ADDRESS OF receiver in 1985

probes.printed: COBOL0900 in-line method invocation id :: "method" requires COBOL-2002 (plus the other OO constructs)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR1  (6.19.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The grammar fixes the roles: sendingOperand admits a literal, function or data reference and receivingIdentifier only a data reference or a special register, so a literal, figurative or function written as identifier-2 is a parse error. The 85-only refusals of the later sender and receiver forms are edition gates beside the rule, each probed.

refuter.evidence: Class c: 2002 literal forms as literal-1 at --std 85: r5hex X"41" -> COBOL0900 hexadecimal literal requires COBOL-2002; r5nat N"AB" -> COBOL0900 national literal (plus COBOL0819); r5bool B"1" -> COBOL0900 boolean literal; r5cat "A" & "B" -> COBOL0900 concatenation. Refusal half: r5lc MOVE X TO "AB" -> COBOL5506. Admission: r5ok (66 RENAMES THRU receiver and sender, two receivers with a comma, ALL literal to numeric, QUOTE, ZERO to a refmod and a numeric receiver) -> [WXYZ] [WXYZ][WXYZ] [777] [""""] [0][000]. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR1 'represents the sending area'.
